h: East End Flavours and Cable Car Views
p: Barking Road runs through the heart of Newham, and the area is famous for its food. Green Street, just up the road, is lined with shops selling saris, jewellery and spices, and Queen's Market at Upton Park is a busy covered market with produce and snacks from around the world. It's a brilliant place to grab a bite after bouncing.

Football fans will know this area as the old home of West Ham United, who played at the Boleyn Ground on Green Street for over a century. The stadium has since been replaced by housing, and the club now plays at the London Stadium in Queen Elizabeth Olympic Park.

South of the area, Newham City Farm in Beckton is a free community farm with animals, and the Royal Docks are where you can catch the cable car that carries you across the Thames to the Greenwich Peninsula with views over the river and the city. It's a fun ride for kids who've never been on a cable car before.
Thames Barrier Park, near Pontoon Dock, has striking gardens and views of the Thames Barrier, the huge flood defence that protects London. Kids are often fascinated by how it works.
East Ham's Central Park is the obvious green space nearby, but if you've got time to explore further, the Royal Docks area has waterside walks and places to eat.
With so many transport links, this part of east London is easy to reach, and it makes a cracking base for a varied day out.
